title: Perfect of imperfectum?
summary: The usage split: perfect for discrete events, imperfectum for description, background and was/had

blocks.title: Twee verledens, één keuze
blocks.body: You now have both pasts — so when do you use which? Rule of thumb: the **perfect** (*ik heb gekocht*) reports a **discrete, completed event** in conversation. The **imperfectum** (*het was, ik had, we woonden*) gives **description, background and habit**. Most stories mix them: perfect for *what happened*, imperfectum for *how things were*.
blocks.callout: *was* and *had* are almost always imperfectum — you rarely say *ik ben moe geweest* to describe yesterday.

pairs.left: Ik heb een fiets gekocht. — I bought a bike.
pairs.right: De fiets was oud. — The bike was old.
pairs.note: Perfect = the event (the buying). Imperfectum = the description (how it was).

pairs.left: We zijn naar Texel gegaan. — We went to Texel.
pairs.right: Het weer was mooi. — The weather was nice.
pairs.note: Perfect moves the story forward; imperfectum paints the scene around it.

pairs.right: Ze was moe. — She was tired.
pairs.note: One completed action (perfect) against a background state (imperfectum).

blocks.prompt: A friend asks what you did yesterday. Which is the natural spoken reply — a reported event?
options: Ik ben naar de dokter gegaan.
blocks.explain: Reporting one discrete event in conversation → **perfect**: *Ik ben naar de dokter gegaan.* *Ik was naar de dokter* isn't grammatical; *ging* would work in a longer narrative.

blocks.title: De was/had-regel
blocks.body: The single most useful habit: **states and feelings in the past go in the imperfectum.** Dutch almost never says *ik ben moe geweest* about yesterday — it says *ik was moe*. Same with *had*: *ik had honger, we hadden geen tijd*. So even inside a story full of perfect-tense events, the *was/had* bits stay imperfectum.
blocks.callout: Quick test: describing how something **was**? Use *was/waren*. Reporting what someone **did**? Perfect is fine.

blocks.prompt: Describe a past state: 'I was tired.'
blocks.explain: *Ik was moe.* Not *ik ben moe geweest* — states stay in the imperfectum.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.scene: Daan leans over his coffee — he wants the whole story of your weekend.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.target: Joh, wat heb je dit weekend gedaan?
lines.en: Hey, what did you do this weekend?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Ik ben naar het strand geweest.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.spotlight: *hoe was het* — now he wants the **description**.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Het was heerlijk. De zon scheen en het was warm.
lines.en: It was lovely. The sun was shining and it was warm.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.target: En toen? Wat heb je gegeten?
lines.en: And then? What did you eat?
lines.spotlight: Back to a discrete event → perfect.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Ik heb een broodje gekocht op de boulevard.
lines.en: I bought a sandwich on the promenade.

questions.q: Why does 'Het was heerlijk' use the imperfectum?
Which line reports a discrete event?

blocks.prompt: Write three lines about a recent day out: one event in the **perfect**, two descriptions (*was/had*) in the **imperfectum**.
